question.problem:
$$
f(y,z)=⟨\text{_____},\,y,\,z⟩
$$

The vector-valued function $f(y,z)$ above parametrizes the hyperbolic paraboloid defined in Cartesian coordinates as $2x=3{y}^{2}-4{z}^{2}.$ What is the first component of $f?$
question.worked_solution:
Solving our equation for $x,$ we obtain

$$
2x=3{y}^{2}-4{z}^{2}\,⟹\,x=\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.
$$

Now, for any point $(x,y,z)$ on our surface, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y,z) & =⟨x,y,z⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2},\,y,\,z⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $y\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the first component of $f$ is $\frac{3}{2}{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.$
